## Extraction notes

*What the schema could not express about this repository. This is the
part of a record worth reading: field values say what fits, these say
what does not — and they are the input to any schema proposal.*

**11 notes.**

### 1.

The sharpest defect in this repository has nowhere to go in the schema: the committed evaluation code cannot produce one of the numbers the documentation reports. The scoring functions (notebooks/01_retrieval_evaluation.py:41-49) test exact string equality between a retrieved chunk's metadata 'source' and the test item's 'source'. Twelve of the 27 items are labelled 'wikipedia_pt' (src/evaluation/test_set.py:5 and eleven others) while ingestion writes 'wikipedia' for every Wikipedia chunk (src/ingestion/wikipedia.py:67, carried to the payload at src/ingestion/run.py:78), so those twelve can never register a hit; a further two are hard-coded to zero for every strategy (notebooks/01:58-64). Thirteen of 27 items are therefore the maximum any strategy can score, a ceiling of 48.1%, and docs/evaluation.md:9 reports Hybrid Hit Rate@5 = 52%. This is neither 'untraceable' nor a conflict 'between two committed documents'; it is a reported figure the committed code makes unreachable, and the schema has no field for it. A field such as reported_figure_exceeds_code_ceiling, or widening document_number_conflicts to cover document-versus-code, would capture it.

### 2.

The same mismatch means the retrieval evaluation is far weaker than retrieval_eval_relevance_rule: source_level suggests: for 14 of 27 items the test is unpassable rather than merely coarse. The schema can say a relevance rule is coarse (more retrievals count as hits) but has no way to say a rule is miscalibrated against the ingested data (no retrieval can count as a hit). Those are opposite failures and both currently read as 'source_level'.

### 3.

interface_kind forces one value where this repository ships three interfaces: a static web chat UI at /, a three-endpoint JSON REST API, and an ingestion CLI. Choosing web_ui discards the fact that the API is separately documented and screenshotted. A list-valued field, or a primary/secondary pair, would fit.

### 4.

The 'no numbers behind the notebooks' finding rests on two independent facts the schema's traceability paragraph treats as one: the notebooks are marimo .py files that store no outputs, and they are also non-executable as committed (no cell imports the names it uses, and every cell's `return` carries no values, so marimo shares nothing between cells). Either alone would make the figures untraceable. Worth noting alongside: pyproject.toml:36 excludes notebooks/*.py from ruff and .github/workflows/ci.yml:27 lints only src/, so CI could never surface the undefined names.

### 5.

Several fields turn on 'shipped', but this repository's shipped behaviour depends on startup order rather than on code alone. hybrid_search.shipped_enabled is recorded true because src/api/routes.py:52-54 calls both retrievers, yet under the documented run order the keyword index is built once from an empty vector store (src/api/app.py:29-51) and never rebuilt, so the sparse list is always empty at request time. 'Present on the request path' and 'actually contributing at request time' are different facts and the boolean cannot hold both.

### 6.

A retrieval-quality difference the schema cannot express: ingestion embeds passages with the e5 'passage: ' prefix (src/ingestion/embedding.py:20) and the ingestion helper embeds queries with 'query: ' (src/ingestion/embedding.py:27), but the request path embeds the query with no prefix at all and with normalize_embeddings=True (src/api/routes.py:17-19), while ingestion does not normalise. retrieval_eval_config_matches_shipped: differs records that eval and shipping disagree, but there is no field for shipping disagreeing with its own ingestion.

### 7.

document_number_conflicts required a scoping decision the schema leaves open: whether a committed screenshot counts as a 'document'. Recorded as 2 with the screenshot included and both sides cited; a markdown-only reading gives 1. Similarly, 'headline number' is undefined, so untraceable_number_count was restricted to reported measurement results and excludes approximations such as README.md:28's '~500MB' and docs/limitations.md:6's '15-30s'.

### 8.

run_instructions: complete and run_instructions_gap_count: 3 sit oddly together — the written procedure names every required category of step and is still unrunnable in three places. The enum measures coverage and the count measures correctness; a reader seeing only the enum would conclude the opposite of what the count says.

### 9.

One further borderline gap was found and deliberately not counted: README.md:19 runs compose in the foreground with no -d, so README.md:22's `docker compose exec` cannot be issued from the same shell. Opening a second terminal is a trivial inference, but a stricter walk-through would return 4.

### 10.

artifacts_unreferenced_count: 0 was reached under a permissive reading. The evaluation notebooks are referenced only as the directory `notebooks/` (docs/evaluation.md:19, README.md:53) and the question set only as the package `evaluation/` (README.md:52); neither individual file path is named anywhere. The checklist asks about artifacts, but the documentation points at their containers, and the schema does not say whether that suffices.

### 11.

No identifying string was copied into this record. Note for the owner: README.md:11-12 contains the repository URL and owner handle, src/ingestion/wikipedia.py:19 embeds the repository slug in a User-Agent string, and pyproject.toml:2 carries the project name. No file path contains a person's name.
